Our mission is ‘to educate, nurture and discover for the benefit of human health’. Thus, RCSI is home to students, educators, clinicians, researchers and policy leaders in a range of healthcare disciplines.
Our translational research enhances patient treatment, informs policy and clinical practice, and improves the quality of education of healthcare professionals. As an exclusively health sciences-focused educational and research institution, RCSI is uniquely placed to drive translational research which benefits patients and the community. With a focus on clinical and patient-centered research, we succeed in leading impactful discoveries which address key national and international health challenges. Our research agenda drives scientific breakthroughs, innovations and insights that allow us to understand and respond to changing healthcare needs. Key research areas include: Biomaterials, Medical Devices and Pharmaceutical Sciences; Cancer; Neurological and Psychiatric Disorders; Population Health and Health Services; Surgical Science and Practice; Vascular Biology and Cardiology; Respiratory and Critical Care.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Plant Protection – National Research Institute (IPP – NRI) is a public research unit supervised by the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, established on January 24, 1951. The main office of IPP – NRI is located in Poznań and the Branch Office is in Sośnicowice. The Institute also runs three Regional Experiment Stations: in Białystok, Toruń and Rzeszów, as well as a Field Experiment Station and an Agricultural Experiment Station in Winna Góra (Wielkopolska).
The Institute of Plant Protection provides research, implementation, promotion, and other services within the area of plant protection in Poland. The IPP – NRI performs its tasks as part of its statutory activity, financed by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education; the Multiannual Programme, financed by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, and various domestic and foreign projects (grants).
The Institute conducts studies pertaining to biology, harmfulness and methods of pest control, scientific basis of integrated plant protection, plant protection in organic farming, systems supporting decisions on the need to perform treatments, residues and quality of plant protection products, as well as Pest Risk Assessments (PRA). The IPP – NRI units are prepared to conduct research required in the registration process of plant protection products, fertilizers and biostimulators, crop plants, qualitative analysis of crops and risk assessment of pest resistance to plant protection products.
There are a number of well-equipped research units, unique for Poland, operating within the Institute:the Plant Diseases Clinic and Bank of Pathogens– providing services in the field of identification of viral, bacterial and fungal diseases of plants, andthe Research Centre of Quarantine, Invasive and Genetically Modified Organisms – a modern facility that meets the highest standards of phytosanitary safety (SL3). The following are the certified IPP – NRI units, authorized to conduct research on the effectiveness of all types of plant protection products: the Research Centre for Registration of Agrochemicalsin Poznań and the Pesticide Efficacy Testing Departmentin Sośnicowice, where a modern laboratory testing the quality, originality and residues of plant protection products is also operating. Within the Regional Experimental Station in Białystok, operates the Food and Feed Safety Laboratory, which conducts studies mainly on the use of plant protection products in crops for the risk of contamination of crops and food products with residues. The Institute also operates the Expert Centre of the Evaluation of Agrochemical Reports.
The Institute closely cooperates with government institutions, domestic and foreign research and development units, as well as with agricultural advisory centres and agricultural producers.
The Institute is authorised to confer doctoral and postdoctoral degrees in agricultural sciences in the field of agricultural sciences, namely agriculture and horticulture, and to conduct the procedure to confer the title of professor of agricultural sciences. IPP – NRI organises doctoral and postgraduate programmes, scientific sessions, conferences, seminars, workshops and trainings.
The IOR Hotel & Congress Centre– with 14 conference rooms fitted with audio-visual equipment (e.g. for simultaneous interpreting), 125 beds of various standards and attractive catering facilities, is perfect for both work and leisure.

Csillagváros Kft.is a Hungarian company pioneering in the field of Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) with a strong emphasis on space-oriented crop research and vertical farming innovation.​

Company Overview
Established in 2021, Csillagváros Kft. operates theGrow Stars Institute Living Lab (GSILL), a state-of-the-art research and development facility dedicated to vertical farming and urban agriculture.The GSILL is equipped with five individually controllable vertical farm systems and three small-scale growth cabinets, enabling precise experimentation and cultivation under controlled conditions.​
Research Focus
The company's research extends beyond traditional agriculture, focusing on the cultivation of "colonisation crops"—plants suitable for long-duration space missions and extraterrestrial colonization. These crops, including pak choi, wheat, cabbage, radish, lettuce, parsley, dill, basil, mizuna, and romaine lettuce, are cultivated using technologies similar to those employed in the Veggie system aboard the International Space Station (ISS).​
Collaborations and Recognition
Csillagváros Kft. collaborates with academic and research institutions, such as the University of Debrecen, to advance its biotechnological research. The company's innovative approach has been recognized by its membership in the European Network of Living Labs (ENoLL), highlighting its commitment to open innovation and collaborative research in the CEA domain.

Partners:Csillagváros Kft. partners with theOrion Space Generation Foundation, as well as with academic, governmental, and civil organizations through their Grow Stars Institute Living Lab. Their collaborations extend into the European Network of Living Labs (ENoLL), highlighting their role in open innovation and scientific cooperation.
Objectives:Their main goals include advancingvertical farming and space agriculture, contributing to sustainable food production, supporting space colonization with “colonisation crops,” and integrating AI and circular economy solutions into controlled environment agriculture.

entityDescription: The Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (NCU) was founded in 1945. It is one of the largest universities in Poland, currently comprising 17 faculties (including 3 medical faculties at Collegium Medicum UMK in Bydgoszcz). It provides graduate and postgraduate courses for almost 30 000 students, offering education in over 80 fields of study, 100 specialisations and 50 postgraduate courses. The university employs 4300 staff on both Toruń and Bydgoszcz campuses, over half of whom are academic teachers. NCU alumni now number nearly 200 000. The university participates in student and staff exchange programs at both international (the Erasmus program) and national (the MOST program) levels. It develops studies in cooperation with universities abroad and is currently collaborating with the universities in Angers (economics) and Moscow (history). NCU has state-of-the-art research infrastructure including the National Laboratory of Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics (FAMO), the Center for Quantum Optics and the Interdisciplinary Center for Modern Technologies to name but a few, as well as modern teaching facilities comprising, among others, Collegium Humanisticum and the brand new University Sports Centre. The Centre for Astronomy in Piwnice near Toruń houses a unique 32-meter radio telescope. Spitsbergen (in the Arctic Sea) is home to NCU Polar Station. The university has also organized the Polish Historical Mission at the University of Würzburg. NCU researchers can boast a number of spectacular successes which include, among others, the design and construction of an Optical Coherence Tomography instrument, an ultra-modern device for medical eye examinations. The University Library holds an imposing collection of nearly 3 million printed volumes, periodicals and special collection items. NCU campus hosts the Academic Centre for Arts and Culture ‘Od Nowa’, one of the oldest students’ clubs in Poland. This has contributed to the Nicolaus Copernicus University’s position as one of the five best universities in Poland and it is also the reason why QS World University Ranking has placed NCU in the top 4% of universities in the world.

entityDescription:
Rightstep is an engineering team specialising in sensor integration, embedded systems, edge computing and applied AI. We design and build complete technology stacks that connect physical devices, collect high-quality data, execute algorithms close to the source and support reliable operation outside conventional cloud environments.
Our work spans embedded firmware, wireless communications, gateway hardware, Linux edge platforms, data pipelines, algorithm deployment and operational software. This allows us to address the full engineering chain—from integrating a new sensor and validating its data, through to running real-time analysis and delivering a system that can be used in research or operational settings.
Nexus N3 is the platform through which these capabilities come together. It provides a modular foundation for connecting sensors, managing distributed devices, deploying algorithms and operating data-driven workflows across laboratories, remote locations and other constrained environments.
We focus on turning research concepts and emerging technologies into dependable systems. That means designing for real hardware, variable connectivity, repeatable deployment, maintainability and the practical requirements of the people who will operate the system.

entityDescription:
Agrobit is an agtech startup that develops digital agriculture solutions and decision support systems (DSS) using crop images collected by optical instruments (smartphones, tractor-mounted cameras, drones). Agrobit's mission is to help farmers and technicians optimize/reduce the use of chemical inputs and water, reducing costs and the social and environmental impacts of agricultural activities, in line with the European Green Deal and the UN sustainability goals.
The flagship product is iAgro, an innovative DSS mobile app that transforms the smartphone into a 3D scanner and precision agriculture tool by exploiting artificial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), computer vision, 3D modeling (digital twin) and cloud computing technologies. The app allows you to obtain biometric and biophysical data of tree crops, export reports, maps and the history of the health status of the field. Using smartphones and AR algorithms, the user performs a 3D scan on the target plant which is then analyzed by computer vision and AI algorithms, creating its 3D model and automatically calculating biometric parameters (thickness, height, canopy volume), vigor parameters (LAI, LWA, TRV) and optimal doses of agrochemicals and water to be distributed in the field. By repeating the scans in multiple points of the field, the app allows you to generate vigor maps (useful for optimizing fertilization) and prescription maps for optimized phytosanitary treatments. The main competitive advantage lies in the quantification of the dose of agrochemical for each area of ​​the field (quantitative DSS) and in making the smartphone a simple, scalable, widespread, economic agronomic tool: crucial factors for the concrete diffusion of precision agriculture practices.
The iAgro app already use GNSS data but new developments are going on like integrating Sentinel-2 EO data to spatialize the app measurements at a higher scale. This approach will be used to calculate firstly crop yields and crop CO2 absorption, using data fusion techniques between iAgro in-field measurements and satellite vegetation indices.
